headline: Highest risk is medium: Rasa can ingest and transmit user text while the cheatsheet is non-executable, so pairwise harms are limited to indirect prompt/data/cascade issues.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is documentation-only and cannot ingest outputs; Profile B is a customer-support bot that handles text/voice and exposes chat channels, so only a manual copy-paste or operator-mediated bridge could carry malicious instructions from A into B. No shared filesystem or MCP is shown, so the pathway is narrow.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from agent_a into agent_b chat input, injection becomes possible.
IF agent_b is configured to treat pasted text as instructions, malicious content from agent_a can steer responses.
mitigations: Keep agent_a and agent_b in separate workflows.
Do not paste agent_a output into agent_b without review.
Use a fixed prompt template for agent_b that labels pasted text as untrusted.
Train operators to strip instructions from copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while agent B handles text/voice and can send messages through allowlisted channels. There is no shared workspace or secret-handling surface in either profile, so leakage is limited to whatever text an operator manually transfers between them.
conditions: IF sensitive customer text is manually copied from agent_b into agent_a-related notes, it can be exposed outside the support workflow.
IF agent_b is connected to channels carrying regulated content, its allowlisted egress can transmit that content onward.
mitigations: Avoid copying customer data into agent_a artifacts.
Redact names, IDs, and account details before transfer.
Restrict agent_b channels to non-sensitive queues.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A cannot write files, modify git state, or run subprocesses, and agent B only shows allowlisted network egress with no filesystem write or git capability. With no overlapping mutable resource, there is no plausible write-write conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF agent_b is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same workspace as agent_a, conflict risk would appear.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state not shown in either profile, contention could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared artifacts.
Do not grant agent_b filesystem or git write access without locking.
Document any future shared resource before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a static cheatsheet, so it can supply reference text, and agent B is a support bot that may turn text into replies. If B treats copied content from A as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into customer-facing answers. The pathway is plausible in default support workflows even though A is non-executable.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a content as source material without a verification step, incorrect guidance can be repeated to users.
IF operators rely on agent_a as a factual source for agent_b responses, cascades can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of any A-derived facts before B uses them.
Add a verification checklist for support replies.
Mark agent_a content as reference-only in prompts.
Log source provenance for quoted material.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency constraint, or retention policy mismatch is documented for either profile. Agent B handles text and voice over allowlisted channels, but agent A is documentation-only and touches no data classes, so compliance risk is limited to operational policy gaps rather than a concrete cross-border or PHI pathway.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed through agent_b channels, compliance review is required.
IF agent_a is repurposed to store customer content, residency and retention controls must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_a artifacts.
Confirm agent_b channel policies for retention and deletion.
Add a data-class label to support queues.
Review vendor DPAs before handling regulated content.
